criteria.evidence: The empty dispatch is replaced by an external_surface pipeline that applies bounds, content mask clip distances and premultiplied blending; native/gpui/checkout carries the applied patch and src-app/src/browser/view.rs:2160 paints the surface on Windows through the shared scene, not through a Windows-only path.

The import checks physical width, height, format, mip levels, array size and sample count, and returns an opaque handle. src-app/src/browser/windows.rs is the only module naming D3D types; the Browser domain sees ExternalSurface plus its generation.

Patches 0010, 0011 and 0012 are declared with the sha256 of the files on disk, verified during this review. The four GPUI revisions in src-app/Cargo.toml and the font-kit feature are untouched by the diff; external_surface_platforms adds windows while the Linux entries and patches 0001 to 0009 stay in place.

presentation.rs is now compiled on Windows, so the 15 FrameConsumer contract tests run on this target and cover pool reservation, import completion, frame intake and release ordering from the harness importer. GPU execution stays attributed to US-008.

The host enables shared textures and implements no on_paint, so there is no CPU refresh fallback. An unsupported format fails in pool_spec with UnsupportedFormat, a stale generation is dropped by the FrameConsumer ledger, and a window without a DirectX surface context refuses page start with an explicit error.

The CEF handle is opened with OpenSharedResource1 inside the callback, validated against the pool description, copied into a host-owned texture and released when the callback returns. The pool textures are shared with DXGI_SHARED_RESOURCE_READ and duplicated only into the client process opened by pid, so the consumer receives bounded rights.

Both sides take key 0 of the same IDXGIKeyedMutex, the producer around CopyResource plus Flush and the consumer around its draw, and a busy key skips the frame instead of blocking. Pool handles are duplicated to the client and closed remotely with DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE; the raw CEF handle is never stored, reused or closed after the callback.

POOL_BUFFERS is 3 and at most two pools coexist, so a replacement holds 6 textures; MAX_PENDING_FRAMES caps in-flight frames at 2. Extra resizes collapse into the single pending_resize slot and the replaced pools are marked retiring, so their generation stops being selected by active_pool.

The callback to publication to consumption path is wired end to end and every exit closes its handles: import_shared_texture closes each handle it consumes, D3dImporter closes the rest on failure, and profile_host_windows closes them when a frame cannot be routed. The FrameConsumer tests cover ownership and release ordering; real fences are observed in US-008.

Device removal, an invalid handle or right, a mismatched description and a retirement older than RETIRE_DEADLINE_MS each emit FrameMessage::Failed with WrongDevice, InvalidHandle, CopyFailed or RetireTimeout. The import runs on a background thread through smol::unblock, and a buffer is only freed when its exact sequence is acknowledged.

Re-read during this review: the log records the DISPLAY1 to DISPLAY2 move, then DISPLAY2 at 150 percent (viewport 1441x881, candidate rect [20,113,12,15]) and at 200 percent (viewport 1266x636, candidate rect [71,113,1,16]), then dpi_restored at 100 percent. The 100 percent candidate rectangles come from the IME corpus of the same run.

The shared modifier mapping sends Ctrl as MODIFIER_CONTROL, which is the Chromium accelerator modifier on Windows, and the platform key stays MODIFIER_COMMAND. Mouse, wheel, key and IME conversions are wired host side; the browser input handler is scoped to the Browser view, so terminal keystrokes are untouched.
criteria.entry_point: BrowserView key and mouse handlers -> Command::Input -> host input()

Menus and the inspector are routed by the shared host client and its DevTools module, and page.rs drops any native event whose document does not match the live document, so a late callback cannot move the focus of another page.

criteria.evidence: The staging builds the client DLL against the same-version CEF development archive at pin 151.3.24 and stages the signed runtime. Verified during this review: the bootstrap, the client and chrome_elf.dll of the campaign bundle all return a Valid Authenticode status for the single certificate CN=Paneflow EP-001 Native Qualification Fresh, while windows-bootstrap.json records the pre-signature build state. Unsigned (target/ep002-unsigned-probe) and untrusted-issuer (target/ep002-untrusted-probe) trios never complete the bootstrap handshake and record created=false. No MSI or public package is involved.

The prototype starts CEF from a separate Paneflow process against the 127.0.0.1:18762 fixture, creates the page (created=true, loaded=true), runs the eight steps and closes the page and its descendants with the sandbox active and exit code 0.
criteria.entry_point: separate Paneflow process -> supervisor -> sandboxed bootstrap
